tasks.prompt: Warm-up: say 事 (si6, low flat tone 低平调) three times in a row. Keep it low and flat, not rising like 試 si3.
tasks.script: 事 si6 · 事 si6 · 事 si6 (compare: 試 si3 is mid-level; 事 si6 sits lower)

tasks.prompt: 60-second self-intro v2, ONE take, no notes: Present → Past → Future (现在 → 过去 → 未来). Include one number and one method. Then check against the script.
tasks.script: I'm an urban analytics graduate from HKU, and I turn spatial data into decisions. Most recently, I worked as a research assistant on an ageing-friendly city project. I built a street-view dataset with about 98% coverage, using Python and ArcGIS Pro, and my analysis helped the team narrow the distance buffer for the regression. Before that, I was the sole analyst on an AI data-centre policy project. Going forward, I'm looking to apply spatial analysis to real planning decisions. That's why this role really appeals to me.

tasks.prompt: STAR #3 Result line, point → reason → example (30 s). Then answer ONE follow-up aloud: 'How did you handle the direction changing?'
tasks.script: As a result, I delivered a baseline analysis of data-centre governance mechanisms from an international perspective, plus a clear list of the data Hong Kong is still missing. (Point.) That matters because it gives future policy work a starting point. (Reason.) For example, the gap list showed exactly which indicators Hong Kong still needs to collect. (Example.) || Follow-up: I kept a written log after every meeting, so everyone agreed on the direction, the deliverables and the deadlines. That stopped rework, because each change was written down. For example, when the scope shifted, I updated the workflow step by step instead of starting again.
